# Operating-system command built from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/command-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data that reaches an operating-system command started with `Runtime.exec` or
`ProcessBuilder` (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta REST):

- a command string, which `Runtime.exec(String)` splits at white space;
- the script a shell runs (`sh -c`, `cmd /c`, PowerShell `-Command`);
- the program to start, or a whole command handed over by the request;
- the environment of the new process.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A shell reads its script as code: a value such as `x; rm -rf /` starts commands of the client's
choosing with the rights of the server. `Runtime.exec(String)` uses no shell but splits the string
into words, so request data in it can still add arguments or choose the program. Environment
variables such as `LD_PRELOAD` can make a fixed program load attacker code.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the host name is appended to a command string.

```java
package com.example.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class PingController {
    @PostMapping("/ping")
    public int ping(@RequestParam String host) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
        Process process = Runtime.getRuntime().exec("ping -c 1 " + host);
        return process.waitFor();
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** a fixed program, with the host as a separate argument after `--`.

```java
package com.example.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class PingController {
    @PostMapping("/ping")
    public int ping(@RequestParam String host) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
        Process process = new ProcessBuilder("ping", "-c", "1", "--", host).start();
        return process.waitFor();
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Start a fixed program and pass request data as separate arguments:
  `new ProcessBuilder("tool", "--", value)`. Use `--` (where the program supports it) so that a
  value starting with `-` is not read as an option.
- Never hand request data to a shell (`sh -c`, `cmd /c`).
- Check values against an allow-list (a `Map.of(...)` of constants or an enum) where you can.
- Do not copy request data into the process environment.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), except a Spring `HttpEntity` or `RequestEntity` (the
  request body and headers); enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as request data.
- A shell is recognised when its name is a string literal first in the command, in a list that gets
  a shell literal added, or in a variable assigned a shell literal in the same method; a shell
  chosen by a ternary, or put into an array element by element, is missed.
- In a list that gets a shell added, every later element counts as shell code. For POSIX shells only
  the element after `-c` is shell code; for `cmd.exe` and PowerShell every later element is.
- Lists and arrays the method builds are judged by their first element; a list filled with `add`,
  with the request value first, is missed.
- Request data as a separate argument of a fixed program is accepted, although a value starting
  with `-` may be read as an option (argument injection, CWE-88).
- One method is analysed at a time and conditions are not evaluated. Allow-list lookups are
  recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants and as `valueOf` of an enum declared in the same
  file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/java/command/command-injection.java`](../../../rules/java/command/command-injection.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
